Last week marked 1 year since @joshdailey joined DocsBot as CGO. And man we've done a lot this year together!

I started making a list for our annual review and it just kept going. With our small team, we've:

- Shipped nearly 90 announced product updates
- Sent 20+ email campaigns and published dozens of blog posts, product announcements, and guides
- Published customer stories with StellarWP, Contractor Foreman, and GravityKit
- Showed up at five conferences
- Ran DocsBot Week with a week of launches, demos, videos, emails, and live builds
- Rolled out a major pricing and packaging update with AI Credits, flexible add-ons, expanded BYOK options, and more flexibility for growing teams
- Rebuilt onboarding with automatic website branding and source discovery, guided dashboard tours, and new free-trial signup paths
- Launched our agency partner program with client handoff and ongoing management, and built out our affiliate resources
- Revamped our SEO, rebuilt hundreds of existing pages, and added roughly 1,000 more pages across industry, integration, comparison, and educational content
- Localized the marketing site into eight languages
- Completed our SOC 2 Type II examination

And then there's the product list 😅

- Deep Research: launched multi-step research across company knowledge, the web, and data analysis. Added question-history research to uncover bugs and documentation gaps, completion notifications, newer models, and usage-based access without a fixed job limit
- Dashboard Operator: introduced an AI assistant that can configure bots, sources, and settings, with interactive questions to guide its work
- MCP: launched our knowledge-search server, private-bot OAuth, question-history access, Admin MCP for managing DocsBot from other agents, and connectors for bringing external tools into DocsBot
- Skills: introduced a plain-language Skill Builder for custom abilities and workflows, plus a library for reusing skills across bots
- Agent API: upgraded reasoning, tool calls, multi-step workflows, and repeated searches so agents can keep working when the first search doesn't answer the question
- AI Actions: added controlled web search, Stripe billing workflows, Calendly/Cal.com/TidyCal booking, and contextual action buttons that turn answers into useful next steps
- Lead collection and CRM: added customizable lead capture, team notifications, and native delivery to HubSpot, Salesforce, Pipedrive, Zoho CRM, and HighLevel
- Voice: launched website and phone Voice Agents in beta, added spoken input to chat, and introduced GPT Live conversations that can listen and speak at the same time
- Messaging channels: introduced Facebook Messenger, WhatsApp, and Telegram integrations in beta
- Slack: added multiple bots per workspace, channel defaults, @ mentions, streaming replies, and support for Actions, Skills, and MCP tools
- Help Scout: improved AI replies with conversation logging, summaries, analytics, customer-property context, and controls for when the AI should stay quiet
- Automation: expanded Zapier, added viaSocket, and introduced webhooks for leads, research, escalations, and ratings
- Data Explorer: built visual exploration of training content and question history to spot topic clusters, gaps, overlapping content, and outliers
- Search and infrastructure: migrated to a new vector database, added U.S./EU storage-region selection, semantic question-history search, and better ranked-chunk inspection
- Document processing: added advanced parsing for complex PDFs and Office files, multi-file and ZIP uploads, individual file processing, and original-file downloads from citations
- Knowledge organization: added Source Tags, filtering, bulk CSV management, custom source titles, and full-file previews
- Knowledge sources: expanded Google Drive and Zendesk controls, and added Zoho Desk, Teamwork[.]com Desk, Salesforce cases, Box, Dropbox, GitHub, Bitbucket Cloud, and Scribe
- Refresh efficiency: added scheduled YouTube playlist refreshes and cached unchanged OCR, image descriptions, and transcriptions to reduce repeat processing costs
- Models: kept adding support from GPT-5.1 through GPT-6.1, expanded our model library and pricing calculator, and lowered AI Credit costs for several newer models
- Dashboard and team management: redesigned navigation, added quick team switching, custom icons, per-bot permissions, metadata inspection, and printable reports
- Chat experience: improved markdown, tables, formulas, diagrams, multilingual text, accessibility, and scrolling. Added dark mode, copy buttons, zoomable images, better branding controls, and live tool/reasoning activity
- Internationalization: expanded the widget to 50 languages with automatic browser-language detection
- Privacy and controls: added browser-side PII redaction and optional confirmation before opening external links
- Developer flexibility: made it possible to update widget options without reloading or interrupting conversations
- Billing convenience: added automatic paid-invoice emails and a separate accounting recipient

Oh, and we built and open-sourced a physical DocsBot robot, gave it an iPhone and Apple Watch remote, and took it to a conference. Because of course the software wasn't enough 😂

Behind all of that were the customer calls, support conversations, demos, onboarding sessions, copy revisions, videos, launch plans, and follow-ups that turn something we built into something people actually use.

I'm grateful to Josh for sharing that load and caring about where we're taking this thing. Having a partner to work through decisions with, challenge ideas, and help get projects across the finish line has made a big difference.

Proud of what this little team shipped this year. Thanks for building it with me, Josh!

👑 EVERY INDUSTRY HAS ITS KING.

Every generation has people who didn’t just enter an industry — they changed the direction of it.

💻 Technology — @BillGates 
Built Microsoft and helped put personal computing into homes and businesses around the world.

📱 Innovation — @SJobs_Stories
Co-founded Apple and helped redefine personal technology through products like the Mac, iPod, iPhone and iPad.

📦 E-Commerce — @JeffBezos
Started Amazon and transformed the way people think about online shopping, logistics and cloud infrastructure.

🚀 Space & EVs — @elonmusk 
Built companies such as SpaceX and Tesla around ambitious goals in space technology and electric vehicles.

💰 Investing — @WarrenBuffett 
Built Berkshire Hathaway into one of the world's most recognized investment companies through a long-term approach to business and capital allocation.

🏀 Sports — @michaelb4jordan 
Became one of basketball's most influential athletes and built a global business legacy around the Jordan brand.

🎬 Entertainment — @DisneyStudios 
Created an entertainment company that grew from animation into one of the world's most recognizable media and entertainment ecosystems.

👗 Fashion — Coco Chanel
Changed modern fashion through designs and a brand that became globally influential.

🏪 Retail — @SamWalton 
Founded Walmart and developed a retail model focused heavily on scale, distribution and everyday low prices.
These people came from different industries.

Different backgrounds.
Different strategies.
Different challenges.
But there was one common idea:

🔥 They didn't just follow the industry. They built something that could move the industry forward.

And now, in the era of Web3, Human Networks, AI, Digital Assets, Payments and Real-World Assets, a new generation of builders is working on what comes next.

🌐 @kv_interlink — Co-Founder of InterLink Labs & Chairman of the InterLink Foundation
KV has been involved in building InterLink from its early stages, and today serves as Chairman of the InterLink Foundation. The Foundation describes its mission around democratizing digital asset ownership, expanding global access, and developing InterLink toward payments and real-world asset infrastructure.

His current role is not simply about building another product.

It's about helping shape a long-term ecosystem.

🌍 1 Billion people.
💳 Global payments.
🏢 Real-world assets.
🤖 AI integration.
🔗 A human-centric blockchain ecosystem.

The Foundation itself describes its long-term vision as making digital asset ownership more accessible and transforming InterLink into an ecosystem for global payments and tokenized businesses.

Of course, no builder can predict the future with certainty.

But history teaches us something important:

The biggest industries were not built overnight.

They were built by people who kept working when the vision was still difficult to understand.

Today, we are watching the early chapters of another technological era.

And I believe the people building during these early days will be remembered for what they created — not simply for what they talked about.

👑 Every industry has its kings.

🌐 Web3 is still writing its history.

And InterLink is building its chapter.

1. STOP TRYING TO DO EVERYTHING.

AI content creation is ridiculously broad.

And one of the biggest mistakes I see beginners make is trying to learn everything at once.

Today you’re creating AI ads.

Tomorrow you’re creating music videos.

The next day you’re doing AI influencers.

Then animation.

Then storytelling.

Then product photography.

Then motion graphics.

Then podcasts.

Before you know it, you’ve touched 15 things and mastered absolutely nothing.

Even something like AI advertising has sub-niches.
You could specialize in:

UGC ads, cinematic commercials, product ads, fashion ads, real estate ads, food ads, storytelling commercials, e-commerce ads…

The same applies to AI storytelling, AI music, image generation and almost every other category.

Pick something.

Become ridiculously good at it.

Give yourself at least 90 days of focused execution before deciding it isn’t working.

You don’t need to become known for everything.

You need people to associate your name with something.
